units.text: Uniqueness results of a nonlinear stochastic diffusion-convection equation with reflection
1 The first section of your paper
Introduction
We want to study uniqueness or, more precisely, comparison principles of solutions of the nonlinear stochastic obstacle problem with additive colored noise
           du − div a(•, u, ∇u) dt + f (u) dt = Φ dW + dη in Q T u(0, •) = u 0 ≥ 0 in D u = 0 on (0, T ) × ∂D u ≥ 0, η ≥ 0 and η(u) = 0,(P)

where the spatial domain D is a bounded Lipschitz domain in R d , T > 0 and Q T := (0, T ) × D. In this sequel, η plays the role of a reflection measure, i.e., η prevents u from becoming negative.The condition η(u) = 0 secures that the reflection is minimal, i.e., η is equal to 0 whenever u > 0. The exact meaning of the expression η(u) is given below.Problems of type (P) have been studied in the past decades in the deterministic case (see e.g.[3]) and for obstacles ψ of Lewy-Stampacchia type in [5,6,8].Stochastic obstacle problems with obstacles ψ of Lewy-Stampacchia type have been studied in [13,15].Therein, existence and uniqueness of a pair (u, η) solving (P) with obstacle ψ instead of 0 has been shown for different types of nonlinear operators and additive forcing f .The construction of the obstacle leads to the fact that the reflection measure η is a functional in L p ′ (0, T ; W −1,p ′ (D)), where p > 1 depends on the nonlinear operator and p ′ = p p−1 .In this case, an Itô formula for the equation in (P) is available, but this theory does not cover the case ψ ≡ 0. The case ψ ≡ 0 has been studied for d = 1 for linear operators − div a(u, ∇u) (see, e.g.[1, 7,9]).In those works, existence and uniqueness of solutions have been studied, where the uniqueness results in [1, 9] heavily rely on the fact that a linear problem is considered, the uniqueness result in [7] a-priori only holds for regular solutions.The uniqueness result therein has been generalized by establishing an Itô formula in [4].We mention that due to the fact that only one spatial dimension is considered, the solution u is continuous with respect to space-time.In higher spatial dimensions the solution fails to be continuous in general.As a consequence, an Itô formula as stated in [4] fails to hold in general which makes it difficult to obtain a uniqueness result in the general case (see Section 3).Moreover, the arbitrary spatial dimension makes it challenging to find a proper meaning to the expression η(u) since η is a non-negative random Radon measure with respect to Q T and therefore η is defined on Borel measurable functions only.Hence, a proper Borel measurable representative of a solution u has to be determined which is non-negative η-a.e. in Q T and satisfies η(u) := Q T u dη = 0. To this end, the theory of parabolic capacity (see e.g.[2,10,11]) has to be used.The existence of a pair (u, η) solving the obstacle problem (P) has been established in [14] under high regularity assumptions on the additive noise term.
Notations and assumptions

For d ∈ N with d ≥ 2 let D ⊂ R d be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, T > 0 and Q T := (0, T ) × D. Moreover we assume p ≥ 2 and p ′ = p p−1 .The closure of C ∞ c (D) in W 1,p (D) will be denoted by W 1,p 0 (D), where W 1,p (D) is the standard Sobolev space.The topological dual of W 1,p 0 (D) will be denoted by W −1,p ′ (D).Moreover, let (Ω, F, P, (F t ) t≥0 , (W t ) t≥0 ) be a stochastic basis with a complete, right continuous filtration and a L 2 (D)-valued cylindrical Wiener process (W t ) t≥0 .The problem of our interest may formally be written as: find a pair (u, η) which is a solution to
           du − div a(•, u, ∇u) dt + f (u) dt = Φ dW + dη in Q T u(0, •) = u 0 ≥ 0 in D u = 0 on (0, T ) × ∂D u ≥ 0, η ≥ 0 and Q T u dη = 0,(1)
where f : R → R is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant L f ≥ 0 such that f (0) = 0 and a : D × R d+1 → R d is a Carathéodory function satisfying the following assumptions:
(A1) Monotonicity: (a(x, λ, ξ) − a(x, λ, ζ)) • (ξ − ζ) ≥ 0 for all λ ∈ R, ξ, ζ ∈ R d and almost every x ∈ D.
(A2) Coercivity and growth: There
exist κ ∈ L 1 (D), C 1 > 0, C 2 ≥ 0, C 3 ≥ 0 and a nonnegative function g ∈ L p ′ (D) such that a(x, λ, ξ) • ξ ≥ κ(x) + C 1 |ξ| p , |a(x, λ, ξ)| ≤ C 2 |ξ| p−1 + C 3 |λ| p−1 + g(x)
for all λ ∈ R, ξ ∈ R d and almost every x ∈ D.
(A3) Lipschitz regularity: There exists C 4 ≥ 0 and a nonnegative function
h ∈ L p ′ (D) such that |a(x, λ 1 , ξ) − a(x, λ 2 , ξ)| ≤ C 4 |ξ| p−1 + h(x) |λ 1 − λ 2 |
for all λ 1 , λ 2 ∈ R, for all ξ ∈ R d and almost all x ∈ D.

Then, the operator W 1,p 0 (D) ∋ u → − div a(u, ∇u) ∈ W −1,p ′ (D) is a pseudomonotone Leray-Lions operator.Moreover, we assume Φ : Ω × (0, T ) → HS(L 2 (D)) to be progressively measurable and Φ ∈ L 2 (Ω × (0, T ); HS(L 2 (D))).In (1) the reflection η is an unknown of the problem and a non-negative random Radon-measure in general.
Notion of a solution
Definition 1.1.A random Radon measure η on Q T is called weak- * adapted if and only if, for any ψ ∈ C c (Q T ) and any t ∈ (0, T ), the mapping
Ω ∋ ω → (0,t]×D ψ(s, x) dη ω (s, x) is F t -measurable.
Definition 1.2.For 2 ≤ p < ∞ we define the space
It is a separable reflexive Banach space endowed with its natural norm
v p W := v p L p (0,T ;W 1,p 0 (D)) + ∂ t v p L p ′ (0,T ;W −1,p ′ (D)) .

Moreover, W is continuously imbedded in C([0, T ]; L 2 (D)) and any v ∈ W admits a cap pquasi continuous representative (see Section 4, Appendix for more details about parabolic capacity and cap p -quasi continuous functions).Its dual space will be denoted by W ′ .
Definition 1.3.Let u 0 ∈ L 2 (Ω × D) be F 0 -measurable and u 0 ≥ 0 a.e. in Ω × D. A pair (u, η) is a solution to (1), if and only if
i.) u ≥ 0 a.e. in Ω × Q T and u ∈ L 2 w (Ω, L ∞ (0, T, L 2 (D))) ∩ L p (Ω; L p (0, T ; W 1,p 0 (D))),
ii.) there exists a right-continuous in time representative of u with values in L 2 (D) satisfying u(t = 0 + ) = u 0 ,
iii.) there exists η ∈ L p ′ (Ω, W ′ ) that is also a weak- * adapted random non-negative Radon measure on Q T with, P-a.s.
∂ t u − • 0 Φ dW − div a(•, u, ∇u) + f (u) = η in W ′ ,
iv.) P-a.s. in Ω there exists a quasi everywhere defined representative of u in Q T , non-negative quasi everywhere in Q T , such that Q T u dη = 0.
